import MilneLib.Sheaf.InvariantModuleBaseChange

/-!
# Composition of ordinary base-change comparisons

The base-change comparison attached to an `R`-linear map is compatible with
composition.  This tensor-level identity is the algebraic input used when
assembling invariant sheaf transitions over nested overlaps.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v w

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace MilneLib.GaloisDescent.SemilinearAction

variable {R T : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing T] [Algebra R T]
variable {M : Type v} {N : Type w} {P : Type u}
  [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
  [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module T P]
  [IsScalarTower R T P]

/-- Extending scalars commutes with composing two linear maps. -/
theorem moduleBaseChangeMap_comp_baseChange
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P) :
    moduleBaseChangeMap R T M P (g.comp f) =
      (moduleBaseChangeMap R T N P g).comp (LinearMap.baseChange T f) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro z
  refine TensorProduct.induction_on z ?_ ?_ ?_
  · simp
  · intro t m
    simp [LinearMap.comp_apply]
  · intro x y hx hy
    simp only [map_add]
    rw [hx, hy]

end MilneLib.GaloisDescent.SemilinearAction
